description: Tata Chemicals' holding in Tata Sons is around 2.5 per cent. Going by the rough-cut valuation, hypothetically, the investment value could be ₹10,000-15,000 crore, as per ICICI Securities.
content: Tata Chem rebounds 14% from intra-day low on huge volume; up 29% in 2 days Tata Chemicals' holding in Tata Sons is around 2.5 per cent. Going by the rough-cut valuation, hypothetically, the investment value could be ₹10,000-15,000 crore, as per ICICI Securities. Listen to This Article Tata Chemicals share price today: Tata Chemicals share price moved higher by 7 per cent to ₹788.50 on the BSE in Wednesday’s intra-day deal. The stock price of the Tata group company bounced back 14 per cent from its intra-day low of ₹690.35 amid heavy volumes. In the past two trading days, Tata Chemicals’ shares zoomed 29 per cent after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rejected Tata Sons' application to surrender its non banking finance company (NBFC) licence, which will force a public listing of the holding company of the salt-to-software conglomerate Tata Group. At 11:14 AM, Tata Chemicals was quoting 2 per cent higher at ₹749, compared to a 0.53 per cent rise in the BSE Sensex. The average trading volumes on the counter jumped multiple-fold, with a combined 15.2 million equity shares, representing 6 per cent of the total equity of Tata Chemicals, having changed hands on the NSE and BSE. What’s driving Tata Chemicals stock price? Last week, the RBI rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its registration as a core investment company, which could pave the way for possible listing of the entity and thereby unlock value. Also Read Tata Chemicals’ holding in Tata Sons is around 2.5 per cent. Going by the rough-cut valuation, hypothetically the investment value could be ₹10,000-15,000 crore, as per ICICI Securities. However, the brokerage firm expects a prolonged legal battle. That said, the stock may remain in positive territory in the short term, it added. ALSO READ: Tata Group firms with stakes in Tata Sons rally on listing expectations Tata Chemicals: Overview, outlook Tata Chemicals is a diversified business dealing in basic chemistry products and specialty products. The company has a global presence with key subsidiaries in the United States of America (USA), United Kingdom (UK) and Kenya, engaged in the manufacturing and sale of soda ash, industrial salt and related products. Tata Chemicals posted a muted performance in the April to June 2026 quarter (Q1FY27), with consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (Ebitda) declining 15 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹560 crore. However, Indian standalone business outperformed, driven by higher volumes in salt and better realisations in soda ash, bicarbonate, and salt. The business is expected to continue delivering healthy performance on the back of resilient domestic demand, stable pricing, and growth-focused capital allocation toward the non-cyclical business. International operations remained weak due to lower soda ash realisations and Chinese pricing pressure. The international business is expected to remain under pressure in the near term due to global soda ash oversupply and higher input and logistics costs, analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services said in the Q1 result update. The near-term environment remains challenging, with the soda ash demand supply balance yet to meaningfully improve despite expectations of future demand from solar glass and electric vehicles. Benefits from these end-use industries are likely to play out gradually, while the current oversupply persists, the brokerage firm said. Further, diversification from the commodity business (primarily soda ash) to the specialty segment/batteries is also expected to pay off for Tata Chemicals in the medium-to-long run, it added. title: How much coral is affected by bleaching?
description: How Much Coral is Affected by Bleaching? Coral bleaching is a widespread crisis. The estimated impact varies greatly, but significant portions of coral reefs globally are affected by bleaching events, threatening marine ecosystems and the livelihoods dependen…
content: Coral bleaching is a widespread crisis. The estimated impact varies greatly, but significant portions of coral reefs globally are affected by bleaching events, threatening marine ecosystems and the livelihoods dependent on them. Coral reefs, often called the “rainforests of the sea,” are incredibly biodiverse ecosystems supporting approximately 25% of all marine life. They provide crucial coastal protection, support fisheries, and contribute significantly to tourism industries. However, these vital ecosystems are facing an existential threat: coral bleaching. Coral bleaching is a stress response where corals expel the symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) living in their tissues, causing the coral to turn white or pale. While corals can recover if conditions improve, prolonged or severe bleaching can lead to coral death and significant ecosystem degradation. The escalating frequency and intensity of bleaching events are directly linked to rising ocean temperatures driven by climate change. The symbiotic relationship between coral and zooxanthellae is the foundation of a healthy reef. The algae provide the coral with essential nutrients through photosynthesis, while the coral provides the algae with shelter and compounds they need for photosynthesis. When corals experience stress, most commonly from elevated water temperatures, they expel the zooxanthellae. This expulsion leads to: - Loss of Color: The vibrant colors of coral come from the zooxanthellae. Without them, the white coral skeleton becomes visible. - Reduced Energy Production: Without the algae’s photosynthetic abilities, the coral’s energy source is significantly diminished. - Increased Vulnerability: Bleached corals are weakened and more susceptible to disease, predation, and other stressors. - Potential Starvation: If the bleaching event is prolonged, the coral will eventually starve. Several factors influence the severity of coral bleaching and the likelihood of coral recovery: - Water Temperature: Elevated sea surface temperatures are the primary driver of coral bleaching. The degree and duration of temperature stress are crucial factors. - Water Quality: Pollution, sedimentation, and nutrient runoff can weaken corals and make them more susceptible to bleaching. - Depth and Light Exposure: Shallow-water corals are generally more vulnerable to temperature fluctuations and light stress. - Coral Species: Different coral species have varying tolerances to temperature stress. Some species are more resilient than others. - Local Adaptations: Some coral populations have evolved greater resilience to heat stress due to previous exposure to bleaching events. Estimating how much coral is affected by bleaching is a complex task. Global assessments rely on a combination of satellite monitoring, in-situ surveys, and modeling techniques. Some key indicators include: - Bleaching Prevalence: The percentage of corals within a reef area exhibiting signs of bleaching. - Mortality Rate: The percentage of corals that die as a result of bleaching. - Geographic Extent: The area of reef affected by bleaching events. - Frequency and Intensity of Events: The number of bleaching events per year and the severity of temperature stress. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and other scientific bodies have warned that even with significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, coral reefs will continue to face severe threats from bleaching. Currently, estimates suggest that over 50% of the world’s coral reefs have already been affected by bleaching events, and this number is projected to increase significantly in the coming decades. Some models predict that under a high-emissions scenario, many coral reefs could experience annual severe bleaching by the middle of the century. While addressing climate change is crucial for long-term coral reef survival, there are also several mitigation and adaptation strategies that can help improve coral resilience: - Reducing Local Stressors: Improving water quality, controlling pollution, and managing fisheries can help corals cope with temperature stress. - Coral Restoration: Active restoration efforts, such as coral gardening and transplantation, can help restore degraded reefs. - Assisted Evolution: Identifying and propagating heat-tolerant corals can help accelerate the natural adaptation process. - Shade and Cooling Techniques: Experimenting with shading structures or artificial upwelling to reduce water temperatures in localized areas. The degradation of coral reefs has profound economic and social implications: - Fisheries: Reefs support crucial fisheries, providing food and livelihoods for millions of people. Bleaching can lead to significant declines in fish populations. - Tourism: Reefs are a major tourist attraction, generating billions of dollars in revenue each year. Bleaching can negatively impact tourism industries. - Coastal Protection: Reefs act as natural barriers, protecting coastlines from erosion and storm surge. The loss of reefs increases coastal vulnerability. - Cultural Significance: Reefs hold cultural and spiritual significance for many indigenous communities. Even individual actions can contribute to protecting coral reefs: - Reduce Your Carbon Footprint: Support policies and practices that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. - Choose Sustainable Seafood: Support fisheries that use sustainable fishing practices. - Reduce Plastic Consumption: Plastic pollution can harm corals. - Use Reef-Safe Sunscreen: Some sunscreen chemicals can damage coral reefs. - Support Conservation Organizations: Donate to or volunteer with organizations working to protect coral reefs. What is the difference between coral bleaching and coral death? Coral bleaching is a stress response where corals expel their symbiotic algae. While bleached corals are weakened and more susceptible to disease and death, they are not necessarily dead. If conditions improve, the corals can regain their algae and recover. However, prolonged or severe bleaching can lead to coral death. Can corals recover from bleaching? Yes, corals can recover from bleaching if conditions improve. The recovery process depends on the severity and duration of the bleaching event, as well as the overall health and resilience of the coral. Factors like water quality, nutrient levels, and the presence of other stressors can influence the recovery rate. Which coral species are most vulnerable to bleaching? Different coral species have varying tolerances to temperature stress. Fast-growing, branching corals, such as Acropora species, are often more vulnerable to bleaching than slower-growing, massive corals. However, there is considerable variation even within species. Are all coral reefs affected equally by bleaching? No, the impact of coral bleaching varies geographically. Some regions, such as the Great Barrier Reef and parts of the Caribbean, have experienced particularly severe bleaching events. Other reefs may be more resilient due to local adaptations or environmental conditions. How does pollution contribute to coral bleaching? Pollution, including nutrient runoff from agriculture and sewage, can weaken corals and make them more susceptible to bleaching. Excess nutrients can promote algal blooms, which can smother corals and reduce light availability. Pollution also contributes to ocean acidification, which can hinder coral growth and resilience. What is the role of climate change in coral bleaching? Climate change is the primary driver of coral bleaching. Rising ocean temperatures, driven by greenhouse gas emissions, are the main cause of mass bleaching events. Ocean acidification, another consequence of climate change, also weakens corals and makes them more vulnerable to bleaching. What are the long-term consequences of widespread coral bleaching? Widespread coral bleaching can lead to significant ecosystem degradation, including: loss of biodiversity, declines in fish populations, reduced coastal protection, and negative impacts on tourism and fisheries. The loss of coral reefs can have cascading effects throughout the marine environment. Are there any natural factors that can help protect corals from bleaching? Yes, some natural factors can help protect corals. Upwelling of cooler, nutrient-rich water can provide a temporary refuge from temperature stress. Genetic variations within coral populations can also lead to increased heat tolerance. Shading from clouds or other natural features can also reduce light stress. What is coral gardening and how does it help? Coral gardening is a coral restoration technique where coral fragments are grown in nurseries and then transplanted to degraded reefs. This helps to restore coral cover and biodiversity in areas where natural recovery is slow or limited. What are some new technologies being used to study and protect corals? New technologies are playing an increasingly important role in coral reef research and conservation. These include: advanced satellite monitoring, underwater robots, genetic sequencing, and 3D printing of artificial reefs. How can individuals help to protect coral reefs in their daily lives? Individuals can help protect coral reefs by: reducing their carbon footprint, choosing sustainable seafood, reducing plastic consumption, using reef-safe sunscreen, and supporting conservation organizations. What is the future of coral reefs if we don’t take action to reduce climate change? If we don’t take significant action to reduce climate change, the future of coral reefs is bleak. Under a high-emissions scenario, many coral reefs could experience annual severe bleaching by the middle of the century, leading to widespread coral death and ecosystem collapse. However, with aggressive mitigation and adaptation efforts, there is still hope for some reefs to survive and even thrive.

title: Glass Wall Systems (India) jumps on market debut
description: Shares of Glass Wall Systems (India) were currently trading at Rs 204.70 at 10:15 IST on the BSE, representing a premium of 12.47% as compared with the issue price of Rs 182.
content: Glass Wall Systems (India) jumps on market debut Shares of Glass Wall Systems (India) were currently trading at Rs 204.70 at 10:15 IST on the BSE, representing a premium of 12.47% as compared with the issue price of Rs 182. The stock debuted at Rs 190.10 on the BSE, a premium of 4.45% over its issue price. So far, the stock has hit a high of Rs 204.90 and a low of Rs 185.05. On the BSE, over 13.21 lakh shares of the company were traded in the counter so far. The initial public offer of Glass Wall Systems (India) was subscribed 81.65 times. The issue opened for bidding on 8 September 2026 and closed on 10 September 2026. The price band of the IPO is fixed between Rs 172 and 182 per share. The offer comprised a fresh issue of equity shares of Rs 2 each, aggregating to Rs 60 crore, and an offer for sale of 20,213,722 equity shares. The offer for sale component consisted of 14,943,048 equity shares sold by India Business Excellence Fund IIA, an investor selling shareholder, and the balance 5,270,674 equity shares sold by the promoters. Of the net proceeds from the fresh issue, the company intended to use Rs 50 crore to fund capital expenditure requirements for setting up a GPU project as part of its planned backward integration at its Vile Bhagad facility, with the balance proposed to be utilised towards general corporate purposes. Also Read Glass Wall Systems (India) was a fade and fenestration solutions provider catering to real estate developers, hospitals, airport authorities, contractors and corporate clients in India, as well as customers in the USA and Australia. The company offered customised fade, curtain wall, skylight, canopy, rain screen cladding, aluminium doors and windows, and other architectural solutions across three verticalsdomestic fade solutions, international fade products supply and fenestration solutions. It had completed 158 projects and had an order book of Rs 981.55 crore as of March 31, 2026. The company operated a manufacturing facility at Vile Bhagad, Maharashtra, with a capacity of 130 panels per day, and was setting up an in-house glass processing unit to support backward integration. Ahead of the IPO, Glass Wall Systems (India) on Monday, 8 August 2026, raised Rs 128.36 crore from anchor investors. The board allotted 70.35 lakh shares at Rs 182 each to 15 anchor investors. The firm reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 83.79 crore and sales of Rs 456.97 crore for the twelve months ended on 31 March 2026. title: Where do the hummingbirds go at night?
description: Where Do Hummingbirds Go at Night? Unraveling the Mystery Hummingbirds, those tiny dynamos of the avian world, vanish as dusk descends. The answer? They primarily enter a torpid state, lowering their metabolic rate dramatically to conserve energy, often perch…
content: Hummingbirds, those tiny dynamos of the avian world, vanish as dusk descends. The answer? They primarily enter a torpid state, lowering their metabolic rate dramatically to conserve energy, often perched on a branch or tucked away in dense foliage, making where the hummingbirds go at night a quest for the carefully sheltered. Hummingbirds are marvels of adaptation, their very existence a testament to evolutionary ingenuity. Understanding their nocturnal habits requires first grasping their daily routine. These energetic creatures are active during daylight hours, fueling their high-metabolic needs with nectar from flowers and tiny insects. This constant need for energy is the driving force behind their unique night-time strategy. Where do the hummingbirds go at night? Ultimately, the answer is directly tied to their need to survive until the sun rises again. The cornerstone of a hummingbird’s nocturnal survival is torpor, a state of dormancy similar to hibernation, but much shorter. During torpor, a hummingbird’s heart rate and breathing slow dramatically, and its body temperature can drop by as much as 50 degrees Fahrenheit. This allows them to conserve vital energy that would otherwise be expended to maintain a high body temperature in the cooler night air. - Reduced heart rate (from hundreds of beats per minute to as few as 5) - Lowered breathing rate (almost imperceptible) - Significantly decreased body temperature While in torpor, hummingbirds are vulnerable. Therefore, they carefully select roosting sites that offer protection from predators and the elements. These locations might include: - Dense foliage within shrubs and trees - Underneath broad leaves, sheltering them from rain - In crevices or sheltered alcoves of buildings (less common) - Sometimes, they reuse the same spot night after night, exhibiting site fidelity Despite their diminutive size, hummingbirds are surrounded by myths and misconceptions. One common belief is that hummingbirds die if they don’t find a feeder at night. While they do rely on nectar for energy, their ability to enter torpor allows them to survive periods without food. Another misunderstanding is that they all migrate south in the winter. While many species do migrate, some remain in their breeding territories year-round, relying on feeders and available nectar sources, even tolerating cold temperatures. This adds nuance to the question of where do the hummingbirds go at night, especially in regions where they are resident. As stewards of our environment, we can take steps to support hummingbird populations. Consider these points: - Plant native nectar-rich flowers: This provides a reliable natural food source. - Keep hummingbird feeders clean: Prevents the spread of disease. Use a solution of 1 part bleach to 9 parts water for cleaning, rinsing thoroughly. - Avoid pesticides: Protects the insects hummingbirds rely on for protein. - Provide shelter: Plant dense shrubs and trees to offer roosting sites. - Keep feeders up late into the evening: This gives hummers that extra boost to make it through the night. Especially if you are curious about where do the hummingbirds go at night? and want to monitor their activity. Despite significant advancements in our understanding of hummingbirds, many questions remain. Researchers continue to investigate the physiological mechanisms of torpor, the factors that influence roost site selection, and the long-term impacts of climate change on hummingbird populations. Advances in tracking technology and physiological monitoring are shedding light on these previously elusive aspects of hummingbird behavior. While both torpor and hibernation involve a reduction in metabolic rate, several key differences exist. Hibernation is a longer-term strategy employed by mammals to survive extended periods of cold weather and food scarcity. Torpor, on the other hand, is a short-term state that hummingbirds use on a daily basis. Mammals often accumulate significant fat reserves prior to hibernation, whereas hummingbirds rely primarily on their ability to rapidly reduce their energy expenditure. Why do hummingbirds need to enter torpor? Hummingbirds have extremely high metabolic rates, requiring them to consume vast amounts of energy. At night, when they can’t feed, they enter torpor to conserve energy and avoid starvation. Without it, they couldn’t survive the night! Are hummingbirds completely unconscious during torpor? No, hummingbirds are not completely unconscious during torpor, but their awareness is significantly reduced. They can rouse relatively quickly if disturbed by a predator or sudden change in temperature, showing that they are still somewhat alert. How can I tell if a hummingbird is in torpor? A hummingbird in torpor will appear motionless, and its breathing will be very shallow and infrequent. They may also be hanging upside down or at an odd angle. Do not disturb them as waking them up expends a lot of their needed energy. Do all hummingbird species enter torpor? Yes, all hummingbird species are believed to enter torpor to some degree. However, the depth and duration of torpor may vary depending on the species, environmental conditions, and individual factors. Do hummingbirds migrate, and how does that affect their roosting habits? Many hummingbird species migrate long distances to find food and breeding grounds. During migration, their need for safe and sheltered roosting locations is even more critical, as they are already expending extra energy. Do hummingbirds always return to the same roosting spot? Hummingbirds often exhibit site fidelity, returning to the same roosting spot night after night, especially if it provides adequate shelter and protection from predators. This behavior can also give clues as to where do the hummingbirds go at night. Can hummingbirds survive cold temperatures? Hummingbirds can tolerate surprisingly cold temperatures, especially when in torpor. Some species even overwinter in areas with freezing temperatures, relying on torpor and available food sources to survive. What is the difference between torpor and hibernation? Torpor is a short-term state of dormancy, while hibernation is a longer-term strategy. Hummingbirds use torpor on a daily basis, while mammals hibernate for months at a time, making the two vastly different. Do hummingbirds dream while in torpor? It is unknown whether hummingbirds dream while in torpor. However, research suggests that brain activity patterns during torpor are different from those observed during sleep, so dreaming is unlikely. Are hummingbirds more vulnerable to predators when in torpor? Yes, hummingbirds are more vulnerable to predators when in torpor, as their reflexes and awareness are significantly reduced. This is why they select roosting sites that offer protection and concealment. How does climate change affect hummingbird roosting habits? Climate change can alter the availability of food sources and the suitability of roosting habitats, potentially impacting hummingbird populations. Changes in temperature and precipitation patterns can affect nectar production and the distribution of insects, making it harder for them to find the resources they need. What should I do if I find a hummingbird that appears to be in distress? If you find a hummingbird that appears to be injured or in distress, contact a local wildlife rehabilitation center for assistance. Do not attempt to handle the bird yourself unless you are trained to do so.

title: L Catterton invests $30 million in Nandhana Foods
description: The investment will support Nandhana Foods’ next phase of growth and enable the group to achieve greater scale by leveraging L Catterton’s industry expertise and operating capabilities.
content: L Catterton, the largest global consumer-focused investment firm, has entered into a definitive agreement to invest in Nandhana Foods, a leading restaurant group specializing in South Indian cuisine. The investment will support Nandhana Foods’ next phase of growth and enable the group to achieve greater scale by leveraging L Catterton’s industry expertise and operating capabilities. L Catteryon has invested $30 million (about Rs 288 crore) for a double digit minority stake in the company, said sources. South Indian cuisine is one of the largest segments of India’s burgeoning food services market. Propelled by secular trends such as the rising per capita expenditure on dining out and food delivery services, as well as the increasing number of consumption occasions, the segment is expected to witness strong growth led by iconic brands like Nandhana Foods. Nandhana Foods has been offering authentic South Indian cuisine for over three decades, with a keen focus on taste, authenticity, food quality, freshness, and menu variety. Together with its unique and customizable spice profile, this dedication has enabled it to cultivate a loyal customer base. Vikram Kumaraswamy, partner, L Catterton said Nandhana Foods’ founding family has built a distinctive and scalable business with a strong consumer proposition and attractive unit economics. It has expanded the business in a disciplined manner and ensured that its restaurants remain anchored in high quality and consistency, he said. There is significant headroom for additional growth by further deepening and broadening its presence in South India and penetrating other markets, he added. Dr R Ravichandar, founder and Managing Director, Nandhana Foods said L Catterton has a profound grasp of the organisational DNA and an intricate understanding of the restaurant industry. “We are excited about tapping into its astute insights and proven know-how to strengthen our operations in line with our commitment to providing high-quality food and service to our customers,” he added. L Catterton has invested in about 30 restaurant businesses till date, with current and past portfolio companies in the space including Dishoom, P.F. Chang’s, Velvet Taco, Baja Fresh, Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen, Cigierre, HUGE, Impresario, and Mendocino Farms. Published on September 16, 2026

title: IPL 2027: BCCI decides to stage mini-auction in India; impact player verdict awaited
description: IPL 2027 auction to be held in India as BCCI ends overseas run after franchise feedback. Decision on Impact Player rule deferred to next GC meeting in a mont...
content: KEY TAKEAWAYS: - The BCCI has decided to hold the IPL 2027 mini-auction in India, moving away from recent overseas hosting trends in Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi. - Venue selection will depend on hotel availability during India's wedding season from October to December, with over 100 rooms needed for franchises. - The Impact Player rule decision remains unresolved, with another Governing Council meeting expected in a month to finalise its future. No more overseas trips! BCCI decides to bring IPL 2027 auction back to India as impact player call deferred The BCCI has reportedly settled on bringing the IPL 2027 mini-auction back home to India, by moving away from the overseas trend that's defined the last few years. According to Cricbuzz, this call came out of Tuesday's IPL Governing Council meeting on September 15, which is one of the biggest takeaways from that sit-down. Ever since the 2023 auction wrapped up in Kochi, the franchises have found themselves flying out for these events, with Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi all taking turns as hosts. That pattern breaks this year, though, as the board has chosen an Indian venue for what will be a mini-auction rather than a full-scale one. However, the bigger mega auction slated for next year might still end up overseas. Franchises had voiced their concerns about the headaches of shipping their entire delegations abroad just for a smaller mini-auction, and this decision seems to reflect that pushback. The BCCI reportedly took stock of these complaints, especially after last year's Abu Dhabi edition left several teams grumbling about logistics and costs. With that feedback in mind, the Governing Council has now agreed to look at Indian cities as potential hosts for this year's event. IPL 2027 mini-auction venue: Wedding season and hotel availability to shape choice BCCI hasn't yet narrowed down on the city. As always, it comes down to whether there's enough hotel space to house all the franchises and their teams comfortably. This year throws in an extra wrinkle as wedding season runs from October through December across India, which tends to gobble up premium hotel inventory fast. So the final venue will hinge largely on which city can guarantee five-star accommodation during that busy stretch. The BCCI's requirement isn't small either: over 100 rooms need to be blocked for at least a couple of nights to pull this off. IPL 2027 Impact Player decision pushed to next meeting On another front, the fate of the Impact Player rule remains up in the air for now. The Governing Council didn't reach a verdict on it during Tuesday's meeting, and instead chose to revisit the topic at another sit-down scheduled roughly a month from now. Interestingly, even though the majority of franchises reportedly aren't fans of the rule, many seem to think scrapping it now would be premature. Several teams have pointed out that their squad-building this season was done with the Impact Player rule firmly in mind, and the omission would put others at an advantage. Their argument boils down to timing, as any call to ditch it should wait until the next mega auction rather than disrupting things midstream. title: Dalal Street faces a double whammy of Fed rate hike, soaring bond yields. Are Sensex and Nifty heading for a bigger crash?
description: Dalal Street faces pressure from rising US bond yields and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike, raising concerns over equity valuations and foreign flows. However, analysts say the impact may depend on earnings growth, currency movements and global li…
content: The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield crossed the crucial 5% mark this week for the first time since 2023. The sharp rise in bond yields came as traders increasingly expect the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates higher for longer, after soaring oil prices revived fears of renewed inflationary pressures. The Federal Reserve is all set to announce the outcome of its FOMC meeting today. The American central bank will likely raise its interest rate, and deliver at least one more hike by the end of March, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters. This comes as price pressures have already been running well above the American central bank's 2% annual target. Also read | Fed rate hike looms as hotter inflation clouds policy outlook Rising bond yields typically make the debt market more attractive to investors, which often leads to some downturn in the equity market. A rate hike by the Federal Reserve also puts pressure on Indian equities. Why analysts advise caution Higher bond yields in developed markets could make emerging-market assets relatively less attractive and potentially lead to capital outflows, said Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities. Also read | Aswath Damodaran calls Fed rate debate pointless, says stock market adapts quickly to higher rates Why Fed rate hike debate may be pointless While stock market traders continue to speculate whether the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates this month and what impact it may have on equity markets, ‘Dean of Valuation’ Aswath Damodaran called the debate pointless, as fundamentals will determine what the American central bank’s decision will be. Before Kevin Warsh took charge as the new Fed chief earlier this year, US President Donald Trump had turned up the heat against Warsh's predecessor Jerome Powell for not reducing the rates. He backed Kevin Warsh, expecting him to cut rates after appointment. But Warsh’s recent commentary seems to be hinting at rate hikes. Trump recently called the members of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee “clowns”. While pressure mounts on Warsh to maintain a balance, Damodaran believes there is little that the Fed chief or even the Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent can do. In a long blog post, he noted that the war in Iran, oil prices and worries around a possible recession have all taken turns driving stock prices in 2026, but the talk around interest rates and where they are going has been a constant concern all year. While investors worry about a possible sharp decline in stock prices due to rising bond yields, Damodaran said it can only happen if the yield increases by more than 3 basis points in one day. He noted that with the S&P 500 went down almost half a percent on days when the 10-year rate increased by more than 3 basis points and up about half a percent on days when the rate decreased by more than 3 basis points. “The secret to equity resilience in the face of higher oil prices, interest rates and political turmoil has been in equity earnings, which have surged over the course of 2026,” he wrote, adding that history has shown that businesses find ways to deliver higher earnings in the face of higher rates, and markets price in these earnings to deliver solid returns, thus adapting quickly. On the soaring bond yields issue, Yes Securities said this reflects higher equilibrium real rate and synchronised global monetary normalisation, rather than deteriorating economic fundamentals or an imminent fiscal crisis. In this background, the domestic brokerage feels a 5% Treasury yield need not be restrictive for equities if corporate revenues and earnings continue to grow, as stronger cash flows can offset a higher discount rate. title: Saudi says Houthis targeted Mecca with a drone, Iran-backed group rejects claim
description: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation condemned the strike as a "heinous" attack. Mecca is Islam's holiest site and the focal point of the annual Hajj pilgrimage.
content: Saudi Arabia said Wednesday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone before it could enter the airspace over Mecca, with the Iran-backed Houthi militia group rejecting the claim as "an worn-out lie," as fighting reaches the holy city for the first time in the ongoing conflict. Turki al-Malki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition which has battled the Houthis since 2015, described the attack as "a deliberate act intended to provoke the feelings of millions of Muslims," and said the holy city's security is a "red line." Mecca is Islam's holiest site and the focal point of the annual Hajj pilgrimage. The Houthis rejected the Saudi statement, with spokesperson Hazem al-Assad saying: "The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone." The Organization of Islamic Cooperation, meanwhile, condemned the strike as a "heinous" attack, denouncing what it described as Houthi attacks on Mecca and the Madinah region alongside the group's "ongoing aggression" against Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia issued a security alert in Mecca on Tuesday, the first since the Houthis last attempted to target the sacred area with a ballistic missile in 2017, after days of intensified attacks that have drawn Saudi Arabia deeper into the Mideast war. The incident marks the latest escalation in the conflict in Yemen, that is testing a month-old defense pact among Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, and adding a new flashpoint to a Middle East already destabilized by the U.S.-Iran conflict. A United Nations-brokered truce in April 2022 largely halted Houthi attacks on Saudi territory, but hostilities have escalated again since the group declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in July and gained control of critical nodes on the country's Bab al-Mandeb coastline. In early September, the Iran-aligned group launched missiles and drones at sites across Saudi Arabia, marking a drastic escalation in the fighting. Riyadh has accused the Houthi rebels of launching attacks on civilian and economic sites in the kingdom. Saudi Arabia has also blamed a pro-Iranian militia based in Iraq for Friday's attack that knocked out the East-West Pipeline, one of the kingdom's most important oil conduits across the Arabian desert, putting 4 million barrels per day at risk and driven a sharp spike in crude prices. The broadening conflict has further rattled oil markets already on edge over the constrained Gulf shipping routes, from a shuttered Saudi pipeline to swings in Strait of Hormuz traffic. Oil prices have climbed alongside the escalation, even as Hormuz flows have been climbing back. While oil was trading lower Wednesday, Brent crude and U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures hovered near four-month highs of $107.8 per barrel and $104.6 a barrel, respectively. The seven-day average of oil transit through the Hormuz Strait rose to nearly 12 million barrels per day as of Sunday — "easily the fastest pace since the post-MOU June-July breakout," according to oil market analyst and founder of research house Commodity Context, Rory Johnston. "This time there's virtually no Iranian crude," he said. Still, that volume remains less than 60% of pre-war levels, Johnston added, underscoring the room shipping through the strait has left to recover as the Yemen fighting and the pipeline outage add fresh risk onto an already-strained supply picture.

title: UK inflation rose to 3.1% in August ahead of Bank of England rates call
description: Figure worsens squeeze on households ahead of BoE meeting
content: UK inflation accelerated to 3.1 per cent in August, worsening the squeeze on households and businesses and keeping open the prospect of a Bank of England rate increase this year. Wednesday’s figure from the Office for National Statistics was above July’s 2.9 per cent reading and in line with the prediction of economists polled by Reuters. Rising petrol prices were the major driver of August’s increase, with higher household energy bills also contributing, the ONS said. The increase takes inflation further above the BoE’s 2 per cent target as the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) prepares to set its key interest rate on Thursday. Economists and traders expect the MPC to hold its rate at 3.75 per cent, but signal that an increase in borrowing costs could come as soon as its November meeting. READ MORE Despite the energy shock from the Iran war, the MPC has resisted lifting interest rates as officials await further evidence on whether higher inflation is becoming entrenched in the economy. The MPC voted 6-3 to hold rates at its last meeting in July, exposing deep divisions on how to respond to surging oil and gas prices. Yael Selfin, chief economist at KPMG, said rising energy prices were likely to test the BoE’s “wait-and-see approach” on rates. “The MPC will be wary of a prolonged period of above-target inflation feeding into significant wage changes and price-setting behaviour,” she said. “There is little evidence of that occurring so far, but without a marked improvement in the outlook, the balance of risks could shift towards a rate rise before the end of the year.” The steep rise in global energy costs has prompted the European Central Bank to raise borrowing costs twice since June, while traders are betting the Federal Reserve will later on Wednesday lift interest rates for the first time since 2023. The blistering rally in oil prices poses a significant political challenge to UK prime minister Andy Burnham, who was swept into Downing Street by Labour MPs on the back of a promise to ease the cost of living for voters. But a steep rise in government bond yields is estimated to have more than halved the government’s fiscal headroom, limiting the scope for giveaways in the October Budget. Responding to August’s figures, chancellor John Healey said: “The war in the Middle East is impacting on inflation worldwide, not just here at home. In our bills, our weekly shop and at the petrol pumps. We have taken early action to help families and give businesses breathing space.” Andrew Griffith, shadow chancellor, took aim at the government for August’s increase, saying: “Inflation is now at 3.1 per cent, meaning that every family is paying the price for Labour’s choices.” Despite the pickup in headline inflation, Wednesday’s data suggested that the spillover of energy prices into the wider economy remained limited – a key point for those MPC members who have voted to hold rates since the Middle East conflict began in February. Services inflation, closely watched by rate-setters as a gauge of domestic price pressures, held steady at 3.4 per cent in August, below economists’ expectations of 3.5 per cent. Core inflation, which excludes energy and food, remained at 2.6 per cent during the month. Official figures on Tuesday underlined the continued weakness of the jobs market and subdued wage growth, with average weekly earnings, excluding bonuses, 2.9 per cent higher in the three months to July compared with a year earlier. Francesco Pesole, strategist at ING, said there was “still no evidence that inflationary pressures are spreading beyond energy [prices]“, which “gives BoE doves something to cling on tomorrow”. Economists cautioned that the expected acceleration in headline inflation in coming months, driven by higher oil and gas prices, could prompt the MPC to raise rates later this year, even if officials resist making further increases. Traders continued to expect a string of rate increases over the coming year, but following the inflation figures, cut bets on a rise at this week’s meeting from 35 per cent to 20 per cent. The 10-year gilt yield fell 0.02 percentage points to 5.38 per cent, and the two-year yield, which is more sensitive to changing interest rate expectations, fell 0.03 percentage points to 4.86 per cent. The pound was slightly weaker at $1.347. CPI inflation is now expected to hit or exceed 4 per cent by early next year – double the BoE’s target. Andrew Goodwin, UK economist at Oxford Economics, said August’s figures offered “no evidence that second-round effects are emerging”, but added that “the pickup in external price pressures has been so great that it looks increasingly likely to force the MPC’s hand”. – Copyright The Financial Times Limited 2026

title: Finance Ministry Debunks 'External Pressure' Myth on UPI Framework
description: The Finance Ministry debunked the 'external pressure' myth surrounding UPI framework revisions, stating policy decisions are made independently for a self-sustaining digital ecosystem and are not influenced by foreign actors.
content: The Finance Ministry debunked the 'external pressure' myth surrounding UPI framework revisions, stating policy decisions are made independently for a self-sustaining digital ecosystem and are not influenced by foreign actors. The Ministry of Finance on Wednesday debunked the "external pressure" myth surrounding the revision in UPI transaction frameworks, clarifying that changes in regulations stem entirely from domestic priorities rather than foreign influence. The Ministry firmly denied allegations that foreign actors shaped the recent policy decisions regarding merchant charges on high-value digital transactions. “Debunking the ‘External Pressure’ Myth: Some claims suggest the change is due to foreign influence. This is false. India’s UPI policy decisions are made independently, with the clear goal of building a self-sustaining, inclusive, and affordable digital payments ecosystem,” the Ministry of Finance stated on X. No Charges for Consumers and Small Merchants The government underscored that the digital payment system continues to be free for everyday consumers across India. Sending money to friends, settling bills at local shops, and scanning quick response codes incur no customer fees. Under the updated framework, person-to-person transfers carry zero charges, irrespective of the amount transferred. The Ministry explained that normal day-to-day commercial transactions remain outside the purview of the new fee structure. Vendors receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month through QR codes operate under a zero-merchant discount rate protection net. Furthermore, the Ministry noted that over 95 per cent of merchant payments stand below the Rs 2,000 threshold, leaving the overwhelming majority of retail volume unaffected. Nominal Charges on High-Value Commercial Transactions Only larger commercial transactions above Rs 2,000 attract a nominal 0.4 per cent charge, an expense borne strictly by merchants rather than retail buyers. To protect the public, commercial banks received explicit instructions preventing merchants from passing MDR costs onto consumers. UPI applications cannot levy separate platform charges. Essential retail services also operate under tightly controlled limits. Payments for railway bookings, fuel stations, telecommunications, utility bills, and insurance services above Rs 2,000 face a capped flat rate of Rs 5 per transaction. Investments in mutual funds and securities transactions attract a 0.02 per cent rate, subject to an upper cap of Rs 300. Fees to Ensure Self-Sustainable and Secure Ecosystem Highlighting the scale and necessity of modernising backend systems, the Ministry cited the platform's exponential domestic expansion since 2016, noting that the network processed 24.5 billion transactions in August 2026 alone. “To keep this system self-sustainable, secure and innovative, a small fee on high-value merchant transactions helps fund: better infrastructure and cybersecurity, support for small merchants in Tier III–VI towns and rural areas, and awareness and incentives to expand UPI adoption,” the Ministry added. The government maintained that the revenue collection structure balances platform upkeep with grassroots economic support. “The new framework ensures resources from higher-value merchant transactions are reinvested to support small businesses and strengthen digital payments across the country,” the Ministry of Finance said. title: AXA CEO Urges Next French President to Tackle Debt With Reforms
description: AXA SA Chief Executive Officer Thomas Buberl called on France’s next president to address the country’s debt mountain with structural reforms and rejected a far-left plan to cancel bonds as “dangerous.” The euro area’s second-biggest economy is under intense …
content: AXA SA Chief Executive Officer Thomas Buberl called on France’s next president to address the country’s debt mountain with structural reforms and rejected a far-left plan to cancel bonds as “dangerous.” The euro area’s second-biggest economy is under intense scrutiny, with a runaway deficit, soaring interest costs and faltering growth. Repairing public finances has become a key issue in campaigning ahead of next spring’s presidential elections. “This new government will have to address the structural issues with reforms in order to get the budget into a better balance,” Buberl told Bloomberg Television on Tuesday. “Increasing taxation year after year will not solve the structural problem.” The head of the Paris-based insurer said there would be a strong reaction from investors if France’s challenges weren’t addressed. The additional yield on French 10-year bonds over their German counterparts, a measure of risk, has already climbed to nearly 1 percentage point, the highest level since Europe’s sovereign debt crisis more than a decade ago. “The risk is then that the markets will show very clearly that they are dissatisfied,” he said. “The message is very clear: there is no opportunity but to restructure the public finances.” French insurers and banks are among the government’s main lenders. AXA has about 12% of its assets invested in the country. Buberl also warned against a proposal from far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon to cancel bonds held at the European Central Bank and the Bank of France. Some surveys of voting intentions show him reaching the second-round runoff. “The discourse around debt and potentially not repaying debt, to my mind this is a very dangerous discussion,” he said. This “plays with fire and plays with the credibility of France.” Photograph: AXA SA CEO Thomas Buberl; photo credit: Chris Ratcliffe/Bloomberg Was this article valuable? title: How do you feed a baby bird without a syringe?
description: How to Feed a Baby Bird Without a Syringe: A Comprehensive Guide Discover effective methods for successfully feeding a baby bird without a syringe, ensuring its survival using alternative tools and techniques. Learn essential tips and tricks to nurture these …
content: Discover effective methods for successfully feeding a baby bird without a syringe, ensuring its survival using alternative tools and techniques. Learn essential tips and tricks to nurture these fragile creatures back to health. Feeding a baby bird that has fallen from its nest or become orphaned can be a daunting task, especially if you don’t have a syringe readily available. While a syringe is often considered the ideal tool for delivering food, it’s certainly not the only option. This guide provides practical and effective alternative methods for feeding baby birds without a syringe, ensuring they receive the nutrition they need to thrive. Before diving into feeding methods, it’s crucial to understand the basic needs of a baby bird. Different species have different dietary requirements, so identifying the bird is helpful, though often difficult. Generally, baby birds require a high-protein diet consisting of insects, worms, or commercially prepared bird formula. - Age is Key: The age of the bird dictates the frequency and consistency of feedings. Very young birds require frequent, small meals, while older fledglings can handle larger, less frequent feedings. - Warmth is Vital: Baby birds cannot regulate their body temperature effectively. Keep them warm using a heating pad set on low or a warm water bottle wrapped in a towel. - Hygiene Matters: Always wash your hands thoroughly before and after handling a baby bird. Use clean feeding tools and prepare fresh food for each feeding. How do you feed a baby bird without a syringe? Several effective methods exist, each with its own advantages and drawbacks. The key is to choose a method that is gentle, accurate, and minimizes the risk of aspiration. - Eyedropper: An eyedropper is a readily available and easily controllable tool for feeding small baby birds. - Pros: Easy to clean, precise dispensing. - Cons: Can be difficult to deliver larger volumes of food quickly. - Small Spoon or Spatula: A small spoon or spatula can be used to gently scoop food and place it directly into the bird’s mouth. - Pros: Readily available, easy to control. - Cons: Requires more skill and patience to avoid spilling or forcing food. - Blunt-Tip Feeding Tube: Although not quite a syringe, a small blunt-tip feeding tube attached to a small plastic bottle can be used to deliver food. - Pros: Safer than a syringe needle, allows for controlled feeding. - Cons: May require some DIY assembly. - Make-shift “Pouch”: Folding a small piece of paper or plastic into a trough can also work. - Pros: Easy to fashion. - Cons: Can be messy, less precise. Regardless of the feeding method you choose, the preparation of the food is paramount. - Commercial Bird Formula: This is the ideal option, as it’s specifically formulated to meet the nutritional needs of baby birds. Mix the formula according to the manufacturer’s instructions, ensuring it is a smooth, lump-free consistency. - Homemade Alternatives (Emergency Only): If commercial formula is unavailable, you can prepare a temporary substitute using ingredients like: - Dry cat or dog food (soaked and mashed) - Hard-boiled egg yolk (mashed) - Mealworms (chopped finely) - Consistency is Key: The food should be thin enough to be easily swallowed but thick enough to avoid aspiration. - Temperature Matters: Warm the food slightly to body temperature before feeding. Feeding a baby bird without a syringe requires a gentle and patient approach. - Prepare: Gather your supplies: food, feeding tool, paper towels, and a warm, quiet space. - Position: Gently hold the baby bird in your non-dominant hand, supporting its body. - Open the Beak: Gently tap the side of the beak or mimic the feeding motions of the parent bird to encourage the baby to open its mouth. - Deliver the Food: Carefully introduce the food into the bird’s mouth using your chosen feeding method. Avoid overfilling the beak or forcing the food. - Observe: Watch for signs of swallowing and allow the bird to finish the mouthful before offering more. - Clean Up: Wipe any excess food from the bird’s beak and feathers. - Repeat: Feed the bird at regular intervals, as needed. Feeding baby birds can be tricky, and it’s easy to make mistakes, especially when learning how do you feed a baby bird without a syringe? - Aspiration: This is the most dangerous mistake. Never force feed or overfill the bird’s beak. Signs of aspiration include coughing, choking, or wheezing. - Overfeeding: Overfeeding can lead to digestive problems. Feed small amounts frequently rather than large amounts infrequently. - Underfeeding: Underfeeding can lead to malnutrition and weakness. Ensure the bird is receiving enough food to maintain its weight and energy levels. - Using the Wrong Food: Feeding the wrong type of food can be detrimental to the bird’s health. Stick to commercial bird formula or approved emergency alternatives. - Hygiene Neglect: Failure to maintain proper hygiene can lead to bacterial infections. Can I use bread to feed a baby bird? No, bread is not a suitable food for baby birds. It lacks the necessary nutrients and can cause digestive problems. Stick to commercial bird formula or approved emergency alternatives. Bread can actually kill a baby bird. How often should I feed a baby bird? The frequency of feedings depends on the age of the bird. Very young birds may need to be fed every 15-30 minutes, while older fledglings can be fed every 2-3 hours. Observe the bird’s behavior and adjust the feeding schedule accordingly. How much food should I give a baby bird at each feeding? Give only small amounts of food at each feeding. The bird’s crop (a pouch in its throat) should be visibly full but not overly distended. How do I know if the baby bird is getting enough food? Monitor the bird’s weight and energy levels. A healthy baby bird will gain weight steadily and be alert and active. What if the baby bird refuses to eat? If the baby bird refuses to eat, try warming the food slightly or gently stimulating its beak. If it continues to refuse, consult a veterinarian or wildlife rehabilitator. Is it safe to use tap water to mix bird formula? It’s best to use bottled or filtered water to mix bird formula. Tap water may contain harmful bacteria or chemicals. How do I keep the baby bird warm? Use a heating pad set on low or a warm water bottle wrapped in a towel to provide warmth. Avoid overheating the bird. What should I do if the baby bird aspirates food? If the baby bird aspirates food, gently turn it upside down and pat its back to help clear its airway. Seek immediate veterinary attention. Can I release the baby bird back into the wild after caring for it? Releasing a hand-raised baby bird back into the wild is a complex issue. Contact a local wildlife rehabilitator for guidance on proper release procedures. What are the signs of a healthy baby bird? Signs of a healthy baby bird include bright eyes, a full crop, active behavior, and steady weight gain. How can I tell what species of bird I have? Identifying the species of the baby bird can be challenging, but a local wildlife rehabilitator or ornithologist may be able to help. What if I find a baby bird and can’t care for it? If you are unable to care for a baby bird, contact a local wildlife rehabilitator or animal shelter. They have the expertise and resources to provide the best possible care for the bird. Knowing how do you feed a baby bird without a syringe? can be crucial in getting it to someone who can properly care for it.

title: NSE IPO: Is India's top exchange a must have in portfolio? Analysts answer
description: NSE IPO will open for bidding on September 17 and close on September 21, looking to raise ₹22,562 crore.
content: NSE IPO: Is India's top exchange a must have in portfolio? Analysts answer NSE IPO will open for bidding on September 17 and close on September 21, looking to raise ₹22,562 crore. Listen to This Article NSE IPO review: At over 40x P/E, the NSE IPO is anything but cheap. Yet brokerages are not walking away from it. Their argument is simple: Investors are paying a full price to get their hands on a market infrastructure with no real substitute. Its leadership position, strong brand positioning, and growing capital market ecosystem make analysts bullish on NSE for both long-term and likely listing gains. Furthermore, its peer BSE commands a steeper valuation of over 50x, on a business less than a third of NSE’s size, strengthening the investment case for the IPO. NSE reported revenue of ₹16,601 crore in FY26 compared to ₹17,141 crore in FY25, reflecting a decline of 3.1 per cent. Ebitda declined 11.1 per cent on a yearly basis to ₹11,265 crore, with Ebitda margin moderating to 67.9% from 73.9% in FY25. Net profit declined 12.2% year-on-year to ₹10,071 crore. Choice Broking said FY26 profit also looks worse than it really is, held down by a settlement charge the company has now paid. Also Read The exchange maintains a dominant position across key market segments with leadership in cash equities, equity futures and derivatives, supported by strong network effects from investors, brokers, institutions and listed companies. NSE IPO will open for bidding on September 17 and close on September 21. A pure offer for sale (OFS) of ₹22,562 crore, the IPO will see 10 shareholders offloading up to 12.64 crore shares. The price band for the NSE IPO is set at ₹1700-1785 per share. Investors can apply for the offer in lots of eight shares. The grey market premium (GMP) for NSE IPO is at ₹156 or 8.74 per cent, suggesting an estimated listing price of ₹1,941. NSE IPO Review Here is what brokerages recommended on the NSE IPO: Choice Broking | Subscribe NSE IPO is priced at 47.3x TTM earnings. BSE, the only listed comparable, trades higher at 48.9x — on a business less than a third of NSE’s size, and on profits helped by the very options volumes NSE has lost, said Choice, adding that buyers are paying full price for the larger and stronger of the two, not a premium over it. "What that price buys is market infrastructure with no real substitute." It said that the main concern is index options. title: More than Half of Consumers are Comfortable with AI Agents Applying for Credit, Experian Research Finds
description: Consumers are moving beyond using AI to research financial products, with growing confidence in AI agents supporting parts of the lending journey, creating new opportunities and challenges for financial institutions. Key findings 54% of consumers are comforta…
content: - 54% of consumers are comfortable with AI agents applying for credit on their behalf. - 82% trust AI to compare loans across providers. - 85% believe AI agents could help compare more options than they could manually. - 84% believe AI agents could help them find better prices or rates. - 75% would feel more comfortable using an LLM connected to a financial institution they already trust. JOHANNESBURG — Consumers are ready to take the next step in their relationship with artificial intelligence (AI), according to AI in Risk: The Rise of Agentic Commerce, new research from data and technology company, Experian, conducted by Forrester Consulting. The study of 6,247 credit-active consumers across 13 EMEA and Asia Pacific markets, found that more than half (54%) of respondents are comfortable with AI agents applying for credit on their behalf. The findings point to the next stage in the evolution of financial services, where consumers are becoming comfortable allowing AI to move beyond providing information to supporting parts of the lending journey, including comparing lenders, checking eligibility, completing applications and securely submitting authorised documents. “Consumers are already changing the way they engage with financial services,” said Mariana Pinheiro, Chief Executive Officer, Experian EMEA & Asia Pacific. “They are not just experimenting with AI anymore; they are beginning to trust it with more meaningful parts of their financial lives. Our research shows that 82% of the surveyed respondents already trust LLMs to compare loans across providers. For banks and lenders, the question is no longer whether AI will influence the next step of that journey, but how to prepare for it while continuing to earn and protect consumer trust. What began as using LLMs to better understand financial products is already moving towards asking AI agents to help them navigate complex financial journeys.” The research found that 85% of the survey respondents believe AI agents could help them compare more options than they could manually, while 84% say AI could help them save money by finding better prices or rates. A further 83% believe AI agents could help them avoid missing important details such as hidden fees or contract terms, while 81% believe AI could reduce decision fatigue by handling research and routine tasks on their behalf. The research also shows that consumers have different comfort levels when it comes to how much autonomy they would give an AI agent. For credit applications, many still want to retain oversight, while other are open to greater delegation: 23% would allow an agent to act when certain pre-agreed rules are met, while 5% would be comfortable giving it full autonomy. Three-quarters (75%) of the respondents said they would feel more comfortable using AI connected to a financial institution they already trust, highlighting the opportunity for banks and lenders to build AI experiences within trusted customer relationships rather than treating AI as a standalone service. As AI agents become capable of carrying out more tasks on consumers’ behalf, financial institutions will need to start preparing systems that support secure interactions between consumer-side AI agents and lender-side platforms. Identity verification, consent management, fraud prevention and explainability will become critical as AI-assisted customer journeys continue to evolve. Experian is helping financial institutions prepare for this evolution through advanced identity, fraud prevention and decisioning capabilities, including Agent Trust, which enables secure interactions between consumers, AI agents and businesses while helping organisations build trusted AI-assisted financial services. title: Fraud Alert: Oregon, Oklahoma enter danger zone after Week 2 setbacks
description: After getting away in Week 1, Oregon can't escape being guilty of fraud in Week 2. There are other teams in the same boat.
content: Fraud Alert: Oregon, Oklahoma enter danger zone after Week 2 setbacks What's the worst thing you can do after being found not guilty in court? Wind up right back in front of the judge. That's the situation facing several college football teams this week. After escaping last week without a conviction, they're back on the docket, once again trying to prove they're not frauds. And unlike Week 1, when optimism and preseason hype still clouded the evidence, Week 2 offered a much clearer picture of who's legitimate and who's been impersonating a contender. One game can be written off. Two games start to establish a pattern. Some teams strengthened their case as playoff-caliber programs. Others looked suspiciously like they spent the entire offseason wearing a disguise and hoping nobody would notice. So with another weekend of evidence now in the books, the USA TODAY Sports District Court is back in session. The charges have been filed. The arguments have been heard. It's time to determine which teams are innocent and which ones are guilty of fraud. No. 6 Ohio State The case: The Buckeyes looked like the No. 1 team in the country for three quarters at Texas, leading 23-3 before a disastrous collapse allowed the Longhorns to pull off the comeback with a last-minute victory. The verdict: Not guilty. The epic meltdown was on par for Ohio State, as it was all self-inflicted with some luck bouncing Texas' way. Jeremiah Smith again proved how deadly he is, and there needs to be a constant effort to get the ball in his hands on top of an already loaded offense. If anything, Ohio State should be glad this happened in the regular season instead of the playoffs. No. 7 LSU The case: Don't let the final score fool you. LSU beat Louisiana Tech 45-14, but that was after it led just 10-7 at halftime after it turned the ball over four times, including three interceptions from Sam Leavitt. The verdict: Jury is still out. After the perfect debut, Lane Kiffin's squad came back down to Earth and showed it's still a work in progress. The horrid first half from Leavitt is concerning as he's not the most prolific passer, but he's been pretty good at taking care of the ball until Week 2. It's going to have to be cleaned up as SEC play begins with a rowdy Mississippi crowd awaiting the Tigers. No. 18 Oregon The case: The Ducks laid an egg in Stillwater, getting completely outplayed by an Oklahoma State team that just lost to Tulsa and had a 21-game FBS losing streak. The verdict: Guilty. Oregon didn't learn its lesson from Week 1. It got away free, only to be found guilty immediately afterward. There are plenty of issues on all sides of the ball, but it all starts with Dante Moore not looking like an NFL-caliber quarterback in a game the Ducks should've coasted through. With the tough schedule awaiting, this looks like it could be Dan Lanning's toughest one in Eugene. No. 19 Michigan The case: The Wolverines responded from the Western Michigan controversy by leaving no doubt in taking down Oklahoma for an impressive ranked win. The verdict: Guilty. While Michigan made a good case in the appeals court, it's conviction remains. Yes, Oklahoma's defense is good, but the Wolverines' benefited from the opponent's mistakes. It still has the sixth-worst scoring offense at 15 points per game while in the bottom 30 of passing and rushing. Defense does win championships, but the offense also needs to carry some of the load. No. 20 Iowa The case: After scoring 40 points in Week 1, Iowa was in another dogfight with rival and rebuilding Iowa State, needing two fourth-quarter field goals to win 16-13 and stave off the upset. The verdict: Not guilty. Save the "Iowa offense is bad" takes. For some reason, the Cy-Hawk game is always a low-scoring affair, as the winner hasn't score more than 20 points in seven of the past eight meetings. That's just how this game goes. The Hawkeyes have shown promise with Tim Lester as offensive coordinator and better outputs are in store. No. 21 Oklahoma The case: The Sooners were held to just 10 points in the loss to Michigan after there was expectation this is the best offense under Brent Venables. The verdict: Guilty. Some things have yet to change in Norman. John Mateer and Co. looked like the thing that held the Sooners back last season from a playoff run, not in sync and unable to run the ball, wondering if it can produce in those big games. The end zone is too difficult of a place to reach when playing against Power conference teams, and that is going to lead to one of the most disappointing seasons in Venables' time. No. 24 Washington The case: The Huskies again had to play all four quarters against a Pac-12 team, fending off a Utah State team that was fresh off a tough loss to FCS Idaho State with a 16-14 win. The verdict: Jury is still out. Jedd Fisch was glad to keep Demond Williams Jr. with Washington, but there isn't much around him to help. The Huskies have clearly been depleted from last season's team and it's resulting in the offense becoming increasingly stagnant and relying on the defense to bail it out. There's time for Washington to get it together, but it needs to show improvement quickly before it's in serious trouble. Mississippi State The case: The Bulldogs went up North to Minnesota and jumped on the Golden Gophers from the jump with a convincing 38-13 win, its first road nonconference win over a Power conference opponent since 2022. The verdict: Not guilty. We have a sleeper in the SEC. Mississippi State looks legit with an extremely talented quarterback in Kamario Taylor leading the way. His gifted arm and legs can take the Bulldogs a long way, with the potential to be a spoiler in some team's playoff hopes while getting his team in the conversation. Illinois The case: Bret Bielema's team blew a 10-point lead at home against Duke, scoring just three points in the second half and losing its first nonconference game at home since the coach's first season in Champaign in 2021. The verdict: Guilty. The things that looked out of sync in Week 1 were on full display in Week 2. The defense has been picked apart in consecutive weeks, not helping quarterback Katin Houser as he has been solid but still adjusting to his new team. The running game has really been a strain, with the new-look offensive line struggling. Illinois has made great strides in football over the past couple of years, but it looks like this will be the campaign it takes a step back. North Dakota State The case: The new FBS team is having little problems adjusting to the level as North Dakota State is 3-0 after fending off a late rally from Air Force for its first Mountain West victory. The verdict: Not guilty. Did we really think the Bison would have problems in FBS? They haven't skipped a beat and look far better than the rest of the conference. You figured it would win a good amount of games, but it's time to start really thinking about North Dakota State winning the Mountain West and being in the playoff conversation, just in Year 1 as football excellence continues in the Fargodome.

title: Global Market | China’s slower loan growth is becoming the new normal: PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng
description: China’s slower loan growth is emerging as a new normal as weakening property and local government sectors reduce credit demand faster than emerging industries can make up for it, PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said. Although new bank lending recovered in August …
content: Pan’s comments come after official data showed that new bank lending recovered in August from a record contraction in July, but remained well below market expectations. Weak borrowing demand from households and businesses continues to weigh on overall credit expansion. Structural shift in China’s credit demand According to Reuters, the slowdown reflects a broader transformation in China’s economy. Lending to the property sector and local government financing vehicles is declining, while newer sectors have not yet generated enough demand for bank credit to fully offset that contraction. China’s outstanding yuan loans stood at more than 280 trillion yuan ($41.73 trillion), with a substantial portion linked to property and local government financing vehicles. As these sectors shrink, maintaining the rapid pace of overall loan growth seen in previous years is becoming increasingly difficult. Pan has argued that the shift does not necessarily indicate a shortage of financing. Instead, the central bank is placing greater emphasis on the quality and efficiency of credit allocation rather than simply expanding the volume of loans. August lending highlights weak demand Household borrowing contracted for a sixth consecutive month, reflecting continued weakness in mortgage demand and limited appetite for debt-funded consumption. From January through August, new yuan loans totalled 10.44 trillion yuan, down from 13.46 trillion yuan during the same period a year earlier. Outstanding yuan loans grew 4.9% year-on-year in August, the slowest pace on record, Reuters reported. Focus shifts beyond bank lending The changing composition of China’s economy is also reducing the importance of bank loans as the sole indicator of financing conditions. Pan has highlighted the growing role of bonds and equity financing in China’s financial system. In 2025, bank loans accounted for 45% of the increase in total social financing, while bond and equity financing together represented 47%, surpassing bank lending for the first time, according to Reuters. The shift is particularly relevant as China seeks to direct capital towards high-tech manufacturing, green industries and other emerging sectors. These businesses tend to rely more heavily on technology, data and intellectual property than on land and physical assets, making them less dependent on traditional bank borrowing. PBOC sees efficiency as key The People's Bank of China has increasingly framed the credit slowdown as part of a longer-term adjustment in the country's financial structure. Pan has previously said that China has moved from an era of rapid economic expansion towards higher-quality growth, meaning the role of finance is increasingly focused on improving the allocation of existing resources rather than continually expanding aggregate credit. According to Reuters, Pan also warned that excessive financial expansion could increase leverage, keep funds circulating in speculative activities and delay the exit of inefficient companies and excess capacity. The policy shift therefore suggests that slower aggregate credit growth may persist even as authorities continue to ensure that viable sectors and businesses have access to financing. The central bank's focus is increasingly on directing capital towards productive uses rather than maintaining a high headline rate of loan growth.
